clue.text: See 29
Ring calling oversight

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
a calling or vocation is a mission

explanation.surface: A phone call that rings unanswered becomes a costly oversight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left out by mistake is an oversight, a thing missed or forgotten.

clue.text: See 23
Fried egg again with last of bacon — one goes "lovely!"

indicators.note: frying an egg scrambles its shape, so the letters are cooked into a new order
goes says the letter standing for one leaves the mix

parts.note: the article a means one

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word bacon

explanation.surface: A breakfast cook frying another egg with bacon, and someone exclaiming in delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one goes' removes an A from EGGAGAIN, and 'last of bacon' adds N; 'Fried' rearranges EGGGAIN plus N into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something charming and attractive can be called lovely; the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: I accept that's a vice!

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins, a vice

explanation.surface: Someone owning up that a habit is a vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you concur with a proposal is a way of signalling acceptance of it.

clue.text: "Kind of Blonde": just a traditional song

parts.note: strawberry blonde is a reddish-blonde hair colour
just in the sense of equitable means fair

explanation.surface: A song title like 'Kind of Blonde' described as merely a folk tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'merely' but means equitable. STRAWBERRY FAIR is an English folk song.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a well-known traditional English folk song about a maid going to a fair.

clue.text: See 14
Upset Noriega has no time for press

indicators.note: has no says a run of letters is removed from the turned name
in a down clue upset turns the word Noriega upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: The former Panamanian dictator Noriega, upset and with no time for the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns NORIEGA into AGEIRON; 'has no time' then removes AGE. Manuel Noriega was Panama's military ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press them flat, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Declaration of one's sexual orientation used in a poem?

definitions.meaning: a person saying they are bisexual, in three short words
iambic feet are metrical units used in verse

explanation.definitionFit: Iambi are metrical feet of an unstressed then a stressed syllable, the building blocks of much verse.

clue.text: Tailored range with baby dolls etc.

indicators.note: tailored means cut and reshaped, so these letters are recut into a new order

explanation.surface: A tailored clothing range that includes baby dolls.
explanation.walkthrough: Baby dolls are short nightdresses, not toys.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby dolls are short nightdresses, so they are examples of clothes worn in bed.

clue.text: Oddly negative old song "No Way He's Eve!", clued cryptically?

parts.note: the old song's title, read as a cryptic clue, rearranges its first four words (its last word, meaning crazy, is the anagram signal) to give these words

explanation.surface: A quizzical description of an old song, retitled as a cryptic clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title is itself a clue: its last word, meaning crazy, signals an anagram of its first four, which makes NO WAY HE'S EVE. 'clued cryptically' says the title is a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1920s novelty song is 'oddly negative' because it says yes and then no in one breath.

clue.text: Fruit's a pain for the walker

parts.note: a corn is a painful patch of hard skin on the foot

explanation.surface: A hard fruit underfoot hurting a walker.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut of the oak tree counts botanically as a fruit.

clue.text: City's rain affected biodiversity

indicators.note: affected means changed or disturbed, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: the word's opening is BIO, its 'diversity' hinting that those letters are mixed too

explanation.surface: Rain affecting the biodiversity of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter splits 'biodiversity' into two parts, the second, 'diversity', acting as a second mixing signal for the first; Nairobi is the capital of Kenya.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Morris's ape was tamed and stuffed with endless knowledge

indicators.note: stuffed with says one piece is packed inside the other
tamed means brought under control and reshaped, so the letters of the word and are reworked
endless says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: ken means knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: A zoologist's ape being tamed and crammed with learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was tamed' turns AND into NAD, which is 'stuffed with' KE (KEN 'endless'). Desmond Morris wrote 'The Naked Ape'.
explanation.definitionFit: Desmond Morris's famous book about humans is titled 'The Naked Ape', so the adjective describes his ape.

clue.text: London's Games near collapsing? Here's a game song

indicators.note: collapsing means falling apart, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the possessive S is kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: Worry that London's Games are about to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here's' is a link. ORANGES AND LEMONS is a London nursery rhyme sung during a children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme naming London church bells is sung while children play an arch-and-capture game.

clue.text: Mean male singer dumping fourth act outside

indicators.note: outside says the act wraps round the shortened singer

parts.note: a deed is an act

indicators.note: dumping fourth says the fourth letter is dropped from the singer

parts.note: a bass is a man with the lowest singing voice

explanation.surface: A mean male singer dropping the fourth act of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Debased and mean both describe something degraded and low in quality or character.

clue.text: Unreliable as a US pickup truck maker?

definitions.text: as a US pickup truck maker?
definitions.meaning: like Dodge, the American maker of Ram pickups, read as Dodge-y

explanation.definitionFit: Something dubious or untrustworthy is described in informal British English as dodgy.

clue.text: Most of family DNA mutates casually in a way

parts.note: kin means family or relatives

indicators.note: most of says the run built from family and DNA loses its last letter

parts.note: the three letters of DNA, mutated, reorder as the name Dan

explanation.surface: Family DNA mutating in some sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutates' turns DNA into DAN; 'Most of' then drops the final N of KINDAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang spelling of 'kind of' means somewhat or in a way, used in casual speech.

clue.text: Persuade someone to buy the drinks

definitions.meaning: to coax or win someone over
to stand a set of drinks for everyone in a group, with the article a inserted

explanation.definitionFit: Get round means coax or win over; heard as get a round it means stand drinks for a group.

clue.text: Part of the brass computer memory device, black in character

indicators.note: in says the memory and black go inside the character

parts.note: tone means character or quality, as of a sound
ROM is read-only memory
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: Computer memory with a dark character in a brass section.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass instrument with a slide, belonging to the brass section of an orchestra.

clue.text: See 18
Blighted with two names, suede's not felt

indicators.note: blighted means spoilt, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so two of them give NN
the possessive S counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: Suede fabric labelled with two names is spoilt, not felt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not felt' looks like a fabric note (suede not felt) but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsensed has not been perceived by the senses, so it was never felt.

clue.text: Ant's companion in the past with ant's heart shape

parts.note: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo, so Ant's partner is Dec
ago means in the past

indicators.note: heart picks the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: Ant's TV partner back in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: ANT McPartlin and DECLAN Donnelly host shows as Ant and Dec in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-sided plane figure is a geometric shape.

clue.text: "The Lady's Covered in Blubber": version of pier song from way back

indicators.note: covered in says the lady is wrapped in the weeping

parts.note: to blubber is to cry
her is the lady's

indicators.note: version of means a rearrangement of the word pier

explanation.surface: A song title about a crying lady, and a pier.
explanation.walkthrough: CHERRY RIPE is an old English song.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a seventeenth-century English song, so a song from long ago.

clue.text: Stages in Tom's total time on earth?

definitions.text: Stages in Tom's total time on earth?

parts.words: Stages in Tom's total time on earth?
parts.note: a tomcat has nine lives, so each is one of nine equal parts

explanation.definitionFit: A cat is said to have nine lives, so each life is one of nine equal fractions of its time.

clue.text: Quaint redundant European body heard a long wandering story

indicators.note: heard says the words are said aloud to sound like the entry

parts.note: quaint is odd, and the EEC is the defunct European Economic Community

explanation.surface: An odd, outdated European institution being listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: ODD EEC said aloud sounds like the answer. The EEC was replaced by the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of Odysseus's travels gave its name to any long, wandering journey or tale.

clue.text: Lights out; insects sound

indicators.note: sound says the insects' name is said aloud

parts.note: fleas are small jumping insects

explanation.surface: Insects making noise once the lights are out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights out' is not bedtime: 'light out' is slang for run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To light out is informal for running off, so it means escapes.

clue.text: See 6
See 11
Architect's unopened grate

indicators.note: unopened says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to grate the teeth is to gnash them

explanation.surface: An architect's grate, never opened.
explanation.walkthrough: John NASH was the Regency architect behind Regent Street and Brighton Pavilion.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash was a celebrated English architect of the Regency period.

clue.text: Spiteful, non-U, volatile and unknown — not the stoic's thing

indicators.note: volatile means unstable, so the remaining letters change order
non-U says the letter U is taken out of the word spiteful

parts.note: y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Describing a spiteful, unstable person unknown to stoicism.
explanation.walkthrough: SPITEFUL less U gives SPITEFL, rearranged as SELFPIT, then Y is added. Non-U is also British slang for not upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic bears suffering without complaint, so wallowing in sorrow for oneself is alien to them.

clue.text: Top cricketer some claim rank handicapped

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some claim a top cricketer's rank is handicapped.
explanation.walkthrough: Imran Khan captained Pakistan to the 1992 cricket World Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a great Pakistani all-rounder and captain, among the top players of his era.

clue.text: Fill out forms ending with "out of date measure"

indicators.note: ending picks the final letter of the word forms

parts.note: an ell is an old unit of length for cloth

explanation.surface: Instructions for filling in forms with an outdated measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fill out' looks like completing forms but means expand.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to expand or grow larger, which is to fill out.
